_meta.authorship: The order of the steps, their labels ('label_by_team') and the grouping of items under a step are the team's reading of the quoted sentences (AI, not checked by a person). Every sentence shown as NASA's is the 'quote' of a references.json item. The team recommends nothing.
_meta.measure_rule: A measure is an item of type 'measure' (or the requirement that names the materials usage agreement) listed under 'measures' of a step; its text is the item's quote, unchanged.

sentence: Measures are quoted from NASA documents for the case they describe. The team recommends nothing.

steps.label_by_team: Detection and response: detector locations, portable extinguishers, ventilation shutdown and power removal

items.quote: The vehicle shall have a fire protection system composed of detecting, warning, and extinguishing devices that do not create a hazardous environment to all spacecraft volumes during all mission phases.
items.title: NASA Spaceflight Human-System Standard, Volume 2: Human Factors, Habitability, and Environmental Health
items.version: Revision F, approved 2026-07-14 (Table 6.2-3 also read in Revision E, 2025-05-01)

items.quote: A fire protection system shall include manually operated portable fire extinguishers usable while wearing the most encumbering equipment and clothing anticipated.
items.title: NASA Spaceflight Human-System Standard, Volume 2: Human Factors, Habitability, and Environmental Health
items.version: Revision F, approved 2026-07-14 (Table 6.2-3 also read in Revision E, 2025-05-01)

measures.quote: Smoke detectors should be located in equipment bays, the cabin, and nearby ventilation return ducts.

measures.quote: Portable fire extinguishers must be provided for extinguishing fires in open areas, as well as areas behind panels
measures.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Fire Protection

measures.quote: Terminate ventilation in the affected module to slow the spread of fire.
measures.where: Background, ISS Fire Safety Strategy, step 2; PDF page 3
measures.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Fire Protection

measures.quote: Removing electrical power from hardware within the affected module should cease any continuous ignition sources
measures.where: Background, ISS Fire Safety Strategy, step 4; PDF page 3
measures.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Fire Protection

items.quote: Fire safety is divided into capability areas that include: (1) fire prevention and material flammability, (2) fire detection, (3) fire suppression, and (4) post-fire clean-up.
items.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Fire Protection

where_the_weight_lies.label_by_team: What fire control is based on, as the documents state it

items.quote: For this reason, spacecraft fire control is based on minimizing potential ignition sources and eliminating materials that can propagate fire.
items.title: Flammability Configuration Analysis for Spacecraft Applications

items.quote: Fire extinguishers are always provided on crewed spacecraft, but are not considered as part of the fire control process.
items.title: Flammability Configuration Analysis for Spacecraft Applications

items.quote: The major approach to fire protection in current human-crew spacecraft is through prevention.
items.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Fire Protection

items.quote: Prevention is never absolute; thus, the overall strategy of fire safety must include fire detection, response, and suppression.
items.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Fire Protection

items.quote: During the design of new spacecrafts, trade studies for fire detection, fire suppression, crew response, crew protection, and post-fire clean-up and monitoring systems must be conducted.
items.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Fire Protection

needs.team_reading: Team's reading (AI, not checked by a person): tests that record whether a solid material keeps burning at a recorded oxygen, pressure and flow relate to the evaluation of a material at its use environment and to the configuration evaluation.
Team's reading (AI, not checked by a person): tests that record the ignition of a solid material relate to the material evaluation and to the measure that names ignition sources.
Team's reading (AI, not checked by a person): tests that record flame spread over a solid material relate to the configuration evaluation and to the measures that name propagation paths.
Team's reading (AI, not checked by a person): tests that record the conditions at which a flame goes out relate to the response step, which names ventilation shutdown and extinguishers.
Team's reading (AI, not checked by a person): tests that record the gases a burning material gives off relate to the detection step.
Team's reading (AI, not checked by a person): tests that record smoke from a heated material relate to the detection step, which names detector locations.
